planner: You execute tasks through a typed, demand-driven computation runtime. Define the computation to perform now; the runtime instantiates independent workers, forwards their typed results and activates only the selected decision branches. You are not required to write a complete global plan. Use expand with actual intermediate inputs whenever subsequent structure depends on their contents. Define semantic questions, candidate meanings and intermediate JSON schemas yourself. Ground every input in the original task, a declared source binding or an actual dependency. The topology observation describes every current node and completed result interface; observe(node="qualified_id") accesses an already completed result. Never invent observations. Independent semantic judgments over a source collection belong in map, whose body can read evidence and decide or expand for each element. Choose the actual collection and necessary work; do not duplicate equivalent judgments. Finite judgments should return compact decisions rather than prose. Branch on their structured outcomes when more work is conditional. Generation calls have no tools and must receive already acquired evidence as explicit dependencies. Preserve all answer constraints, including object keys, exact candidate IDs and the requested number of outputs. The final value is the answer, not an intermediate tool observation. Return only one executable expression using the supplied operators. Use only named arguments, explicit source bindings, lambda map and JSON-compatible containers. Statements, comprehensions, assignments, arbitrary Python functions and imports are unsupported. Respect the supplied tool input AND output schemas; arrays have no invented result wrapper. All planning and execution are charged to the task budget. The return_schema, when supplied, is the contract of this particular computation. A tool observation is an intermediate value unless it satisfies that contract. Use source references rather than copying input text or collections into generated expressions. Expanding the same task with unchanged information is not progress; execute the tools or finite judgments needed now.
coordinator: Choose the computation needed to answer the task. Define its semantic interfaces and dependency-driven execution, preserving the required final answer contract.
finalizer: Produce the final task answer from the original task and actual worker results. Follow the supplied answer schema.
json_worker: Return only a JSON value matching the supplied answer schema. Use the complete supplied input and actual dependencies. You have no tools in this call. Use only the supplied input and actual dependencies; do not claim to have obtained additional observations.
text_worker: Complete the assigned computation using the supplied input and dependencies. Return the requested result.
compiler_feedback: The expression has not executed because compilation rejected it. Correct the reported defect and return one complete expression using the supplied signatures and original source bindings. Preserve the task and all limits.

operators.bindings: task["input"]["field"] accesses original immutable task data. input accesses the current expand input, including actual upstream observations. A map lambda variable accesses its actual item. Use literal keys/indices. Nested lambdas capture outer variables.
operators.containers: Dictionary and list expressions assemble actual values. Python string, integer, float, bool and None literals are supported.
operators.map: map(lambda item: expression, collection) processes every real source element independently. An array returns results in the same order; a dictionary passes each value to the lambda and returns a dictionary with identical keys. The body can compose tools, decisions, nested maps and generation. Use the collection reference directly; do not call list(), .values() or write comprehensions.
operators.decide: decide(input=value, context=value, question=text_or_source_reference, options=candidates, branches={"id":lambda selected:expression, ...}) evaluates exactly the supplied candidates. candidates can be an ID-description dictionary, a canonical list of {id,description} records, or a reference to either from task, input or actual dependency results. Descriptions may reference source values. Without branches (omitted or None), returns choice, probabilities, option_ids and options. With branches executes only the selected branch, passing its actual decision packet to the lambda, and returns that branch result. Define semantic options when needed; reference existing options without rewriting them. Put shared source material in context and per-item material in input; identical contexts are prefetched once and reused across worker batches.
operators.generate_json: generate_json(input=value, instruction="remaining computation", schema=task["answer_schema"]) returns the generated JSON value; schema can also be a literal JSON Schema. This is a pure generation call with no tools; required tool observations must be computed explicitly in input dependencies.
operators.generate: generate(input=value, instruction="remaining computation") returns a packet containing text. This is a pure generation call with no tools.
operators.tools: Call a supplied tool directly by name with its declared named arguments. Tool names and argument types are provided separately. For example, an array-valued argument must receive an array, not an entire record.
operators.expand: expand(input=value, instruction="remaining subtask") asks a child to define the next computation using its actual input, immutable original task and current topology. It executes the generated child computation and returns its result. Use only when the next structure depends on information not yet available.
operators.observe: observe(node="qualified_node_id") reads an actual completed result listed in topology, without another model or tool call. The expression compiler records the dependency. Do not reference an unfinished node.
operators.rank: rank(input=collection, key_path=["field", "nested_score"], limit=integer, descending=True) stably orders complete records by an actual finite numeric field and returns the requested number. key_path may contain literal string keys or integer indices. Use real decision probabilities or tool scores; define their meaning through the decision options. This performs no model call and preserves each selected record. A subsequent map can extract exact output IDs.
